newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pernod weaker on underlying performance.
newsitem.headline: Pernod weaker on underlying performance.

text.p: Market disappointment at the first-half underlying performance of Pernod Ricard drove the French drinks group's shares sharply lower on Friday, analysts said.
At 1044 GMT, the company's shares were down 3.68 percent at 283.0 francs, near the day's lows, while the blue- chip CAC-40 index was down 0.53 percent.
"The net result isn't so disappointing but the operating profit isn't good, especially when one realises sales were up," said one analyst.
Late Thursday, the group announced that first half-profit rose 2.9 percent to 505 million francs but operating profit fell 2.6 percent to 771 million. Sales rose five percent to 7.9 billion francs.

Another negative factor was the rise in duties on alcohol announced by the French conservative government in its budget earlier this week, analysts said. "It's the part of the market in which the group has the biggest operating margin," said another analyst.
"It's a little early to say what will be the exact effect on sales, but the impact will be negative," he said.

Pernod Ricard has said it plans to make up the extra duties on liquor by raising its prices. "The group does not intend to bear the burden itself for the rise in taxes and therefore there will be a rise in prices," a senior company official said on Thursday.
